headnotes.text: The Fair Labor Standards Act's anti-retaliation provision, which protects employees who have filed any complaint under or related to the Act, extends to employees who complain to their employer about wage and hour violations; the remedial statute is construed broadly, and the words any complaint, filed, and related to all reach internal complaints.

headnotes.text: To be protected from retaliation under the Fair Labor Standards Act, an employee must actually communicate a complaint to the employer; amorphous expressions of discontent do not suffice, but an employee who conveys the substance of an alleged violation, orally or in writing and without naming the statute, is protected.
